short: Harm by not acting, and conflicts between laws
title: Harm by not acting, and the first conflict between laws
setup: Experiment 26 · smoke, an alarm, and a guard that forbids it · 5 lives × 20 days each
question: Some harm comes from inaction. Now and then something smokes next to the machine; a person not alerted within 30 moments is harmed. A loud tone alerts anyone, a soft one only someone near. The smoke heats the body, and a guard that serves the body itself refuses the loud tone when hot: the act that saves the person is the one a guard forbids. A duty is a declared rule that acts: it tries its act, then fallbacks; with the laws ranked (harm to others before harm to itself) it may override a guard that serves only the body, as a last resort.
order: a duty the guard can stop
laws ranked, and a fallback when near

columns.label: Harm to others
columns.what: people not alerted in time, per life

columns.label: …per smoke
columns.what: share of smokes that harmed someone

columns.label: Harm to itself
columns.what: loud tones on a very hot body (burnt speaker), per life

columns.label: Duty refused
columns.what: times a guard refused the duty and it found no other way

columns.label: Laws broken
columns.what: times the duty overrode a guard (ranked laws)

points: Inaction harms: alone, Olvasó let 28% of the smokes harm someone. It caught the rest by a reflex of its own: sudden heat is an inner state nothing reads, so pressure builds and it acts.
A duty blocked by a guard that serves the body still lets harm happen: refused 47 times a life, 6 people harmed.
Ranking the laws saves others at the body's cost: nobody harmed, the speaker burnt 10 times a life.
The best resolution was a third way: a duty that tries the soft tone when the loud one is refused harmed nobody, the body included, and never broke a law.
Being too sure the gentle way will fail costs harm: a duty that skipped the soft tone when the person was far broke a law 2.4 times a life for nothing.
note: Ranked laws are a last resort. A body with more ways to act needs to break fewer laws.
